- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after recent price spikes (especially >72.5) — cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 1–2 points.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70.5), model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5 points to catch the rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices — add 0.5–1.0 point bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.5 to -1.5 in 3–5 days), model reacts too slowly — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
